# `prefer-empty-slice-len`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `std.mem.eql` or `mem.eql` comparisons where one operand is an empty
string literal `""` or empty slice `&.{}` instead of checking `.len == 0` or
`.len != 0`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Comparing against an empty slice literal via `std.mem.eql` involves a function
call, slice length checks, and potential pointer comparisons. In Zig, testing
whether a slice is empty is idiomatic, faster, and clearer by checking
`slice.len == 0` (or `slice.len != 0`).

## When it fires

Whenever validating whether a string or slice contains elements.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn isEmpty(name: []const u8) bool {
    return std.mem.eql(u8, name, "");
}
```
